meta.thesis: Allbirds does not need a new shoe - it needs to prove the two things only it can claim: measured carbon footprint per shoe and all-day comfort, and Walk Lighter makes the label the message.

business_problem: Allbirds invented sustainable sneakers and watched everyone copy them: FY2024 revenue fell ~25% to ~$190M from a $297M peak, stores closed, and 'the eco shoe' lost differentiation while the comfort claim - its real retention driver - got buried under sustainability messaging [S1][S2][S3].

Capture 650 email/SMS signups via comfort-test events and the carbon-receipt funnel

findings.finding: SEC filings show revenue down ~25% YoY to ~$190M with ongoing net losses - the decline is documented, not inferred; the brand has a real turnaround plan in progress
Comfort is the dominant organic theme in customer reviews ('cloud', 'all day', 'no break-in') - retention runs on feel, not mission
Allbirds already prints a carbon footprint score per product - a unique, measurable asset almost no competitor has; it is invisible in marketing
Copycat 'eco sneakers' (Nike Move to Zero, generic wool shoes) blurred the category - 'sustainable' no longer differentiates without numbers

assumptions.text: Gross margin ~45% on DTC footwear (from 10-K reported margins)
$5,500 paid social at ~$8 CPM = ~690K impressions + ~210K organic
8 comfort-test event shifts at ~$350 each (venue, fitting chairs, signage)
LIGHTER15 code: $15 off first pair; netted in revenue
Repeat purchase ~25% within 12 months (comfort loyalists buy multiple pairs)

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: Allbirds invented the eco sneaker - then everyone copied it. Revenue fell ~25% to ~$190M while 'sustainable' stopped meaning anything [S1][R4].
Solution: Walk Lighter - prove the two things only Allbirds has: a printed carbon score per shoe and cloud-level comfort, at live comfort tests everywhere.
45-day goal: 140 orders, 650 captures, +12 pts 'most comfortable, measured' [O1-O3].
slides.notes: Sell the fit, not the shoe.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Tree/Wool Runners: merino + eucalyptus sneakers, $98-135, famous for all-day comfort [S2][R2].
Unique asset: a printed carbon footprint score on every product - measurable sustainability no rival matches [R3][S2].
ReRun resale program exists - circularity is real, not marketing [S2].
Reviews run on 'comfort/cloud/all-day' - the retention driver is feel [R2].
slides.notes: Hold the shoe up - 'the tag has a number on it. The number IS the campaign.'

slides.title: Company & Position
bullets: Public DTC footwear company (NASDAQ: BIRD) - filings document a real decline and a transformation plan [S1][S3].
Category is crowded: Nike, On, Hoka all claim 'sustainable' - differentiation died [R4][S4].
Positioning gap: 'eco shoe' is generic; 'the shoe with a measurable footprint' is unclaimed.
Campaign claims the proof.
slides.notes: Public company - the decline is in SEC filings, not our opinion.

Baseline: current list; week-0 survey; Shopify code report.

P2: eco-conscious millennials + gift buyers 28-50 - mission-driven, carbon-aware [R3].
P1 buys the comfort; P2 buys the number.

slides.title: Research Methodology & Results
bullets: SEC filing analysis: Allbirds 10-K - revenue, margins, store count, transformation plan [R1][S1].
Shelf audit of 8 sources: product/carbon-label pages, ReRun, Nike/On/Hoka positioning [S2][S4].
Review spot-check: ~300 on-site review themes - 'comfort/cloud/all-day' dominates [R2].
Measurement plan: pre/post intercept survey (n=150) runs as week-0 baseline [M1].

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: [R1] Revenue -25% is documented -> this is a turnaround brief, not an awareness brief.
[R2] Reviews run on comfort -> lead with feel: comfort tests, not eco lectures.
[R3] Carbon score exists but is invisible -> make the label the campaign: 'every shoe has a number'.
[R4] 'Sustainable' is generic -> sell proof (measured carbon) not adjectives.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Theme: Walk Lighter - lighter footprint, lighter on your feet; proof, not claims.
Push-pull: comfort tests create the try-on (pull); carbon receipt + club convert at home (push) [R2][A4].
Transparency as the weapon: a printed number beats a green adjective [R3][R4].
PESO: paid geo-social, earned trade-in PR, shared comfort tests, owned email/SMS + comfort club.

slides.title: Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $14,650: paid social $5.5K [A4]; creators $2.4K [A6]; events $2.8K [A7]; production $600 [A10]; LIGHTER15 fund $2.1K [A8]; contingency ~9% [A11].
Funnel: 900K impressions x 2.6% CTR x 0.6% purchase = ~140 orders = $15.4K revenue [A1][A4].
GP 45% = $6.9K; direct ROI ~-53% - a turnaround-proof budget; payback via 25% comfort-loyal repeat [A2][A13].
Conservative (50%): 70 orders, ROI ~-76%; kill-trigger protects the downside [A15].

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: Allbirds is the rare brand with a real, documented decline - and a real, provable asset nobody's using.
Walk Lighter sells proof, not mission: a printed carbon score and a comfort claim you can test on the spot.
Judges hold the shoe and see the number - the pitch is the product.
